requirements.text: The business must maintain a register of business entities, the umbrella concept covering all customers, vendors and employees.
Each business entity must be identified by a single company-wide business entity number that is unique across every party, regardless of whether the party is a customer, a vendor or an employee.

The business entity number must be usable to link a party to information held in other areas of the business (sales, purchasing, HR), with the party register acting as the integration point for the company.
requirements.obj: party to information in other business areas

requirements.text: The business must be able to recognise that the same party may play more than one role at the same time (for example an employee who is also a retail customer), and the system must not force a party into a single role.
Each business entity record must carry a last-changed timestamp recording when it was last updated, so the business can understand the currency of the party register.

Each business entity carries a globally unique record identifier that exists only to support data replication between systems; it has no business meaning, is not a business key, is treated as technical metadata and needs no business reporting.
The business must record every person it deals with, identified by the same company-wide business entity number as the business entity.
Every person is a business entity and has no separate identifier of their own, while not every business entity is a person.
The business must record the primary type of each person, which classifies why the person exists in the company's systems.
The recognised primary person types are store contact, individual (retail) customer, salesperson, employee (non-sales), vendor contact and general contact.
The business must be able to count, segment and filter people by their primary type in every analysis, for example the number of individual customers held in Germany.
The list of person types is a small fixed set of codes held in the person record itself rather than in a separate reference list.
The warehouse must present the meaning of each person type code in business language rather than as the two-letter code.
The business must record each person's first name, middle name or middle initial, and last name.
The business must record an optional courtesy title (for example Mr. or Ms.) for each person for use in correspondence.
The business must record an optional surname suffix (for example Sr. or Jr.) for each person.

The business must record a name style for each person indicating whether the name is presented in western order (first name then last name) or eastern order (last name then first name), as a presentation rule for correspondence and reporting.
Any report or output that displays a person's full name must be able to honour the recorded name style and must not assume western ordering.
requirements.obj: person full name according to name style

requirements.text: Middle name, title and suffix are optional, and reporting must cope with people who have none of them.
The business must record each person's email promotion preference, which expresses the consent given for marketing contact.
The recognised email promotion preference levels are: no email promotions, email promotions from AdventureWorks only, and email promotions from AdventureWorks and selected partners.

Marketing and campaign selection must be able to filter by email promotion preference and distinguish the company-only case from the company-and-partners case, because the two permit different uses of the person's details.

Because consent is compliance-sensitive, the business must be able to state what a person's email promotion preference was historically and not only its current value, so historical tracking of consent changes must be introduced by the warehouse if an audit trail is required.
The business must retain additional contact information held for a person in a free-form structured (XML) format.
The business must retain demographic information collected from online shoppers, such as hobbies and income, which is captured for sales analysis.
Demographic content must be made analysable, for example for segmenting customers by income band or interest, rather than stored as an opaque block.
Access to demographic and additional contact information must be treated as sensitive and restricted separately from ordinary name and contact reporting.
Each person record must carry a last-changed timestamp so the business knows how current a person's details are and can identify records not touched for a long time.
The business must record the email addresses of people.
A person may have more than one email address, each numbered within the person, and the business must be able to report all of a person's email addresses.
An email address belongs to exactly one person and is meaningless without that person.
The business must be able to identify people who have no email address, since they cannot be reached by email campaigns regardless of their promotion preference.
Each email address must carry its own last-changed timestamp so the business can see when a person's email details were last touched independently of the rest of the person record.
The warehouse must retain superseded email addresses historically so the business can tell whether an address currently on file is still the one previously used in a campaign.
The business must record the telephone numbers of people.
A person may have several telephone numbers, and each number is qualified by the kind of phone number it is.
The business must maintain a reference list of phone number types, each with a name describing the kind of number (for example home, work or mobile).
Reporting must be able to select a person's telephone number by type, for example the work number of every store contact in Bavaria.
A telephone number belongs to exactly one person.
Each recorded telephone number must carry its own last-changed timestamp.
The business needs consistent naming of phone number types over time, because renaming a type changes the meaning of historical reporting.
The business records a sign-in credential for a person, consisting of a protected (hashed) password value and the random value used to protect it.
Credentials must never be brought into the warehouse as readable values, reported on, or exposed to analysts.

The only business-relevant facts about a credential are whether a person has one and when it was last changed, which indicate whether the person has a self-service account and how recently they maintained it; if the business does not need these facts, the credential record should be excluded from scope.
One person has at most one credential, and the credential is attached to the person by the same business entity number.
The business must record postal addresses, each identified by its own address number.
An address consists of a first street address line, an optional second street address line, a city, a postal code, and the state or province in which it sits.
The state or province determines the country, so the country of an address is known indirectly through its state or province rather than being stated on the address itself.

The business must record the geographic location (latitude and longitude) of an address to support mapping, distance and territory analysis, such as showing reseller stores on a map or measuring how far customers are from a store.
Addresses must be reportable at each geographic level: street, city, postal code, state or province, and country or region.
Each address carries a last-changed timestamp so the business can see when address details were corrected.

An address is recorded once and can be shared by more than one party, for example several employees of the same reseller store or a household; the business must not assume an address belongs to a single party.

The business must decide whether historical address values must be retained, so that past activity can be reported against the address as it stood at the time, given that address records can be edited in place and later corrections may affect analysis of where a customer was at the time of a past order.
The business must record which addresses belong to which business entity (party) and in what capacity.
A party can have several addresses, and the same address can serve several parties.
Every party-address relationship must carry an address type stating the role the address plays for that party, for example Billing, Home or Shipping.
A party may have different addresses for different purposes, for example one address to bill and another to ship to.
The combination of party, address and address type makes a party-address relationship unique.
A party may hold the same address under two different address types, for example as both billing and shipping address, and both must be visible.
The business must maintain a reference list of address types, each with a descriptive name.
The business must be able to answer what the shipping address of a given customer is.
The business must be able to answer which customers ship to a given city.
Each party-address relationship carries its own last-changed timestamp.
The source holds only the currently valid set of party-address relationships, as parties move and add and drop addresses.
If the business needs to know which address a party used at a given point in the past, the warehouse must build and keep that history, because the operational system will not supply it.
The business must be able to identify parties with no address on file, since they cannot be shipped to or invoiced by post.
The business must maintain a reference list of countries and regions, each identified by its ISO standard country or region code and carrying its name.
The business must maintain a reference list of states and provinces, each identified by its own number and carrying an ISO standard state or province code and a descriptive name.
Every state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.
A country or region may contain many states or provinces, and some may contain none.
A state or province carries a flag indicating that no genuine state or province code exists for that entry and that the country or region code is being used in its place.
Reporting must handle the no-genuine-code flag gracefully and must not present a substituted country code as if it were a real state code.
Every state or province is assigned to a sales territory, linking where an address is to the part of the sales organisation responsible for it.
The business must be able to roll addresses, and therefore customers, stores and employees, up to sales territory via their state or province, to support territory-level sales and coverage reporting.
Only the assignment of a state or province to a sales territory is available in this area, so the warehouse must obtain territory descriptions from the sales area.
The business can change the territory assignment of a state or province, and reassigning a state to a different territory retrospectively changes every historical geographic roll-up.
The business must decide whether territory assignments should be tracked over time, so that past performance can be reported on the territory structure that applied at the time.
requirements.obj: tracking of territory assignments over time

requirements.text: The country, state and territory reference lists each carry a last-changed timestamp.
Country and state or province names used in customer-facing output and reporting must be consistent and current, and renames must be visible rather than silent.
The business must record which people act as contacts for which organisations, for example the named individual who is the contact at a reseller store or at a supplier.
A contact relationship links two parties: the organisation (a business entity) and the person acting as its contact.
Every contact relationship must carry a contact type describing the role the person plays for that organisation.
The business must maintain a reference list of contact types, each with a descriptive name.
The same organisation may have several contacts, each in a different role; the combination of organisation, person and role makes the contact relationship unique.
The same person may act as a contact for more than one organisation and may hold more than one role at the same organisation.
The business must be able to answer who the contact at a given store is and in what role.
requirements.obj: contact and role at an organisation

requirements.text: The business must be able to answer which organisations a given person represents.
Each contact relationship carries its own last-changed timestamp.
The source holds only the current set of contact relationships, although contact roles change frequently as people move jobs.
If the business needs to know who the contact was at a given time, for example when investigating a past order, the warehouse must retain that contact history.

Reporting must clearly distinguish which side of a contact relationship is the organisation and which is the individual; since the relationship itself does not label them, the distinction must come from the party's role.
requirements.obj: organisation and individual in contact relationship

requirements.text: The business needs a single view of a party that brings together, for one party number, the party's name and type, all email addresses, all telephone numbers with types, all addresses with types, and all organisations the party is a contact for.

Reporting must correctly reflect that a party's addresses, emails, telephone numbers and contact relationships are one-to-many, and must not assume a person has exactly one address, email or phone number.
The single view of a party must remain correct when a party plays several roles at once.
Every record in this area carries only a last-modified timestamp, and the operational system holds the current state only and overwrites previous values in place.

The business currently has no history for person names, marketing consent, email addresses, telephone numbers, address details, party-address usage, organisational contacts, or state or province territory assignments, all of which change and matter analytically.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of a person's name, so that past activity can be reported against the details that applied at the time.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of a person's marketing consent.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of a person's email addresses and telephone numbers.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of an address's street, city and postal details.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of which addresses a party uses and for what purpose.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of who is a contact for an organisation and in what role.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of which sales territory a state or province belongs to.
The last-changed timestamp on each record is the only change signal the source provides, and its reliability needs to be confirmed with the operational system owners.
The source provides no deletion marker or status flag anywhere in this area, so a party, address or relationship removed operationally simply disappears.
The business must state whether removals of parties, addresses or relationships need to be detected and retained.
The business needs visibility of people without an email address.
The business needs visibility of people without a phone number.
The business needs visibility of people without any address.
The business needs visibility of duplicate people, meaning the same individual registered more than once under different party numbers, because this affects customer counts and campaign accuracy.
The business needs visibility of addresses whose geographic location is missing, since these cannot be mapped or measured for territory purposes.
Reporting should highlight states or provinces carrying the no-genuine-code flag rather than hide them, as they signal incomplete geographic reference data.
requirements.obj: states or provinces with no genuine code

requirements.text: Reference lists (address type, contact type, phone number type, country or region, state or province) must be complete, so that every relationship and address resolves to a named type, country or region.
Unresolvable references to types, countries or regions must be reported as a data quality defect.

This area holds personal data about identifiable individuals, including names, home addresses, private email addresses, telephone numbers, geographic coordinates, marketing consent, and self-declared demographics including income.
Access to person-level detail must be restricted to roles with a legitimate business need.
Aggregated reporting, such as counts by region, by person type and by consent level, should be available more widely.
Sign-in credentials must be excluded from all analytical use.
Marketing consent must be respected by every downstream use of the data, including any extract that leaves the warehouse.
The distinction between consent for 'our company only' and 'our company and partners' must be carried through to any data sharing decision.
The business must be able to answer, for an individual, what personal data it holds about them across this area, supported by the single view of a party.
requirements.obj: personal data held about an individual

requirements.text: The company-wide party number is assumed to be stable and never re-used for a different party; this must be confirmed with the operational system owners.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 states each business entity is identified by a single company-wide, unique business entity number across all parties; REQ-003 uses it as the integration point, and REQ-077 assumes stability (to be confirmed). Satisfies unique, recognised, non-null and stable criteria.
REQ-007 and REQ-008 state a person is identified by the same company-wide business entity number and has no separate identifier; REQ-045 reinforces this. Unique, business-recognised and non-null.

REQ-030 and REQ-031 say an email address is numbered within the person and is meaningless without the person, so the key is the composite of person number and the within-person sequence. EmailAddressID is only a local sequence, so confidence is moderate.
The address text is recognised by the business (REQ-029), but REQ-034 says addresses are superseded over time, so it is not stable. Uniqueness is not stated either.
REQ-035, REQ-036 and REQ-039 say a person may have several numbers, each qualified by type, and each number belongs to one person. No explicit identifier is given, so the composite is inferred.
REQ-037 describes a reference list of phone number types with a name, but gives no explicit identifier. The ID is a reference code and is the only stable handle in the source columns.
REQ-037 describes types by name (home, work, mobile). REQ-041 warns that renaming changes meaning, so the name is not fully stable.
REQ-001-2 states each postal address is identified by its own address number. The business recognises it, and REQ-007-2 says one address is recorded once and shared.
REQ-015-2 and REQ-011-2 describe an address type reference list (Billing, Home, Shipping) with a descriptive name. No identifier is explicitly stated, so this is the reference code.
REQ-015-2 gives each address type a descriptive name that the business uses. Names can be renamed, so stability is weaker.
REQ-013-2 explicitly states that party, address and address type together make a party-address relationship unique. REQ-010-2 and REQ-014-2 support the composite.
REQ-022-2 states each country or region is identified by its ISO standard code. The code is stable, unique and recognised by the business.
REQ-022-2 gives the country name, but REQ-034-2 says names are renamed over time, so it is unstable.
REQ-023-2 states each state or province is identified by its own number. It is unique and non-null.

REQ-023-2 gives an ISO state or province code, and REQ-024-2 ties each state to one country. REQ-026-2 says a genuine code may be missing, so the code can be substituted and is not reliably non-null or unique on its own.
REQ-039-2 explicitly states that organisation, person and role together make the contact relationship unique. REQ-036-2 and REQ-037-2 support the three parts.
REQ-038-2 describes a contact type reference list with descriptive names. No identifier is explicitly stated, so this is the reference code.
REQ-038-2 gives each contact type a descriptive name that the business uses. It can change over time, so stability is weaker.

REQ-012 says person types are a small fixed set of codes held in the person record, and REQ-010 lists them. They are stable codes but have no separate reference table, so this is a classification code rather than a main business key.
REQ-006 explicitly says the globally unique record identifier exists only for replication, has no business meaning and is not a business key. It is technical metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_details
satellites.description: Business entity register change timestamp; rowguid excluded as replication-only technical metadata.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_name
satellites.description: Person name details with full history.
satellites.split_rationale: Ordinary personal name data; carries the Person last-modified timestamp (held in this satellite only).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_type
satellites.description: Primary person type classification code.
satellites.split_rationale: Classification used for wide aggregated reporting; changes at a different rate from names.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_consent
satellites.description: Email promotion (marketing consent) preference with full history for compliance audit.
satellites.split_rationale: Compliance-sensitive consent tracked independently of name changes.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_person_sensitive
satellites.description: Sensitive XML additional contact information and demographics, access-restricted.
satellites.split_rationale: Data classification: sensitive personal data restricted separately; XML data type.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_email
satellites.description: A person's email addresses, numbered within the person, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_phone
satellites.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type, with history.
satellites.split_rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person).

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_credential
satellites.description: Existence and last-change date of a sign-in credential only; hash and salt are never loaded.
satellites.split_rationale: Separate source; credential values excluded for security.

satellites.name: sat_address_details
satellites.description: Street, city and postal details of an address with full history.

satellites.name: sat_address_location
satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of an address for mapping and territory analysis.
satellites.split_rationale: Spatial data type and personal-data classification differ from street details.

satellites.name: sat_address_type_details
satellites.description: Address type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_contact_type_details
satellites.description: Contact type descriptive name.

satellites.name: sat_phone_number_type_details
satellites.description: Phone number type name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_country_region_details
satellites.description: Country or region name, historised so renames are visible.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_details
satellites.description: State or province ISO code, no-genuine-code flag and name.

satellites.name: sat_state_province_territory
satellites.description: Sales territory assignment of a state or province, historised; territory descriptions come from the sales area.
satellites.split_rationale: Territory reassignment changes at a different rate and drives historical roll-ups.

satellites.name: sat_business_entity_address_details
satellites.description: Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship.

schema.name: ModifiedDate

schema.name: ModifiedDate

contracts.name: BusinessEntity

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity. This is the business key for the asset.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row in the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: BusinessEntityAddress

schema.name: BusinessEntityID

schema.name: AddressID

schema.name: AddressTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the type of address (the role the address plays for the entity). References AddressType.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier from the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: BusinessEntityContact
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset linking a business entity to a person acting as a contact, qualified by a contact type. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key integrity; value-level constraints are left for producer/consumer review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (e.g. a vendor or store) that the contact belongs to; references BusinessEntity.

schema.name: PersonID
schema.description: Identifier of the person who is the contact for the business entity; references Person.BusinessEntityID.

schema.name: ContactTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the type/role of the contact; references ContactType.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row, used for replication/row identification.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: ContactType

schema.name: ContactTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the contact type; business key of the ContactType reference table.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the contact type (the role a contact holds).

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: CountryRegion
contracts.doc: Reference data for countries/regions, sourced from the CountryRegion source table and landed in staging. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: CountryRegionCode
schema.description: Code that identifies the country or region; the business key of the asset.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the country or region.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: EmailAddress
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for email addresses associated with a business entity (person). Each row links a BusinessEntityID to an email address identified by EmailAddressID. The contract enforces the declared schema, business-key primary key and not-null rules; value-level semantics are advisory pending producer/consumer review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (person) that owns the email address; references the BusinessEntity/Person record.

schema.name: EmailAddressID
schema.description: Identifier of the email address row, distinguishing multiple email addresses for the same business entity.

schema.name: EmailAddress
schema.description: The email address string for the business entity.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row, used by the source system for replication.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the row was last modified in the source system.

contracts.name: Password
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for the Password table, which holds credential data (password hash and salt) for a business entity (person). The contract enforces the declared schema, business key and not-null rules deterministically; value-level semantics are not yet specified by requirements and are left for producer/consumer negotiation. Contains sensitive credential data and should be reviewed for access and handling.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (person) to which this password record belongs; references the BusinessEntity/Person record.

schema.name: PasswordHash
schema.description: Hash of the password for the business entity. Sensitive credential data; not the plain-text password.

schema.name: PasswordSalt
schema.description: Random salt value used when computing the password hash. Sensitive credential data.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row, used as a row-level unique identifier by the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time when the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: Person
contracts.doc: Staging contract for the Person source table: one row per individual (employee, customer contact, vendor contact, etc.) identified by BusinessEntityID. Enforces the declared schema, business-key uniqueness and not-null rules; value-level semantics are minimal because no further requirements were stated. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity this person belongs to; business key of the Person record and reference to BusinessEntity.

schema.name: PersonType
schema.description: Code indicating the type/category of the person (source column PersonType). Allowed values not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: NameStyle
schema.description: Flag indicating how the name is written/ordered (source column NameStyle). Exact value semantics not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: Title
schema.description: A courtesy title for the person (source column Title).

schema.name: FirstName
schema.description: The person's first (given) name.

schema.name: MiddleName
schema.description: The person's middle name or initial, if any.

schema.name: LastName
schema.description: The person's last (family) name.

schema.name: Suffix
schema.description: Name suffix for the person (source column Suffix).

schema.name: EmailPromotion
schema.description: Email promotion preference indicator for the person (source column EmailPromotion). Allowed values not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: AdditionalContactInfo
schema.description: Additional contact information for the person (source column AdditionalContactInfo). Format not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: Demographics
schema.description: Demographic information about the person (source column Demographics). Format not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) for the source record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: PersonPhone
contracts.doc: Staging contract for PersonPhone: the telephone numbers associated with a person, together with the phone number type (e.g., cell, home, work). Each record links a person (BusinessEntityID) to a phone number and its type. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint; schema, primary-key and not-null breaches are enforced by the deterministic core.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Identifier of the business entity (person) that the phone number belongs to; references the Person/BusinessEntity record.

schema.name: PhoneNumber
schema.description: Telephone number of the person, as recorded in the source system.

schema.name: PhoneNumberTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the kind of phone number (e.g., cell, home, work); references PhoneNumberType.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: PhoneNumberType
contracts.doc: Reference/lookup data describing the types of phone numbers (e.g. cell, home, work) that can be associated with a person's phone number. Sourced from the PhoneNumberType source table and staged as-is; the contract enforces the declared schema, primary key and not-null rules. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: PhoneNumberTypeID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the phone number type; referenced by PersonPhone.PhoneNumberTypeID.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the phone number type (e.g. the category of phone such as cell, home or work).

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: StateProvince
contracts.doc: Source-to-staging asset for StateProvince: state or province reference records, each linked to a country/region and a sales territory. The contract enforces the declared schema and business-key constraints; value-level semantics are left for producer/consumer review.

schema.name: StateProvinceID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the state or province record.

schema.name: StateProvinceCode
schema.description: Code identifying the state or province.

schema.name: CountryRegionCode
schema.description: Code of the country or region the state or province belongs to; references CountryRegion.

schema.name: IsOnlyStateProvinceFlag
schema.description: Flag indicating whether the record is the only state/province for its country or region (i.e., StateProvinceCode is not used).

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the state or province.

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory the state or province belongs to.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (ROWGUIDCOL) for the row.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified.

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 122 requirement(s) and 20 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (7)

- **hub_business_entity** — business key `BusinessEntityID`. Company-wide party register (customers, vendors, employees, persons). A person is a business entity with no separate identifier, so persons share this hub rather than getting a hub of their own. Email, phone and credential relations are also keyed by BusinessEntityID and feed this hub. Integrated from 5 source(s): BusinessEntity.BusinessEntityID, Person.BusinessEntityID, EmailAddress.BusinessEntityID, PersonPhone.BusinessEntityID, Password.BusinessEntityID; canonical staging key column `BUSINESSENTITYID`. _(requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-045, REQ-047, REQ-049, REQ-077)_
- **hub_address** — business key `AddressID`. Postal address, recorded once and shareable by many parties. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-007-2)_
- **hub_address_type** — business key `AddressTypeID`. Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping). _(requirements: REQ-011-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-068)_
- **hub_contact_type** — business key `ContactTypeID`. Reference list of contact roles a person plays for an organisation. _(requirements: REQ-037-2, REQ-038-2, REQ-068)_
- **hub_phone_number_type** — business key `PhoneNumberTypeID`. Reference list of phone number kinds (home, work, mobile). _(requirements: REQ-037, REQ-041, REQ-068)_
- **hub_country_region** — business key `CountryRegionCode`. Country or region identified by ISO code. _(requirements: REQ-022-2, REQ-068)_
- **hub_state_province** — business key `StateProvinceID`. State or province identified by its own number. _(requirements: REQ-023-2, REQ-068)_

### Links (4)

- **link_address_state_province** — connects hub_address, hub_state_province. The state or province in which an address sits; country is derived via the state. Unit of work: AddressID + StateProvinceID from Address. _(requirements: REQ-002-2, REQ-003-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-055)_
- **link_state_province_country_region** — connects hub_state_province, hub_country_region. Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region. Unit of work: StateProvinceID + CountryRegionCode from StateProvince. _(requirements: REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-005-2)_
- **link_business_entity_address** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_address, hub_address_type. Party-address relationship in a given capacity (address type); unique by party, address and type. Unit of work: BusinessEntityID + AddressID + AddressTypeID from BusinessEntityAddress. _(requirements: REQ-009-2, REQ-010-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-016-2, REQ-017-2, REQ-020-2, REQ-056)_
- **link_business_entity_contact** — connects hub_business_entity (organisation), hub_business_entity (contact_person), hub_contact_type. Organisational contact relationship: an organisation (BusinessEntityID), the person acting as its contact (PersonID) and the contact role; unique by all three.
